newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian stocks take heart as Yeltsin op nears.
newsitem.headline: Russian stocks take heart as Yeltsin op nears.

text.p: Russian shares closed higher in light volumes on Wednesday after doctors said President Boris Yeltsin could undergo his heart operation next week, traders said.
"The sooner the operation takes place the better as it will give answers to many questions," said Alexei Genkin of Alfa-Kapital.
U.S. heart specialist Micheal DeBakey said the operation could take place as early as next week.
But Nikolai Fomintsev of Analaiz said there had been almost no Western buying and domestic investors had taken the opportunity to mark up prices.
"There was almost no activity from companies working with foreign investors...In the absence of Western orders, domestic traders succeeded in talking prices up," he said.
Fomintsev said the low interest of Western investors was explained by recent bad news from Russia and the fact that many players had quit the market at its last peak.
UES rose to $0.0809 from $0.0804 at Tuesday's close, Rostelekom rose to $2.55 from $2.47 and Norilsk Nickel rose to $6.42 from $6.24.
